pathways.name: Sell before expiry
pathways.summary: Convert an illiquid, single-tenant, single-site asset into cash or into a diversified position while a lease is still in place.
drivers: Sale proceeds are priced off the remaining lease term; the shorter the term at sale, the more the buyer discounts.
Measure ULA can take 4.00% or 5.50% of gross consideration if the site is inside the City of Los Angeles and the price clears the threshold.
System same-store sales fell 1.1% in Q3 FY2026 and the company guided to 50 to 60 closures in fiscal 2026.
A § 1031 exchange is available for real property and can defer the gain if the owner wants to stay in real estate.
risks: Sale certainty depends on a cap rate no government source publishes; the achievable price is unverifiable here.
Transfer tax, recapture and exchange deadlines make the execution path unforgiving.
Selling crystallises the tax today rather than at an unknown later date.

pathways.name: Renew with the incumbent tenant
pathways.summary: Extend the existing operator and keep the income stream, at a rent and term the tenant will actually sign.
drivers: Unemployment in the Los Angeles metro area fell to 4.4% in September 2026 from 5.5% a year earlier, and nonfarm payrolls rose 0.5%.
Education and health services grew 3.8% year over year and carry 1,340.7 thousand jobs, the largest sector in the metro.
The issuer's own filings describe a shrinking footprint and falling franchise rental revenue, which weakens the tenant's negotiating posture on rent.
Median household income in Los Angeles city is $81,939 and in the county $90,112, supporting local consumer demand.
risks: A renewal that pushes the total remaining term, counting options, to 35 years or more creates a change in ownership and a reassessment under California law.
The tenant is closing 50 to 60 restaurants in fiscal 2026 and has discontinued its dividend and buyback; credit is deteriorating, not improving.
Population in Los Angeles County is 3.2% below its 2020 estimates base, a demand headwind for marginal sites.
A renewal does not remove the concentration risk: one site, one operator, one intersection.

pathways.name: Short extension, then sell
pathways.summary: Buy time with a short, clean extension that preserves a marketable remaining term, then take the asset to market from a position of strength.
drivers: A sale is worth more with a signed term certain than with a looming expiry, so a short extension can be value-accretive even at a modest rent.
Keeping the total remaining term, including options, strictly under 35 years avoids the leasehold reassessment trigger.
The ten-year Treasury at 4.84% sets the risk-free anchor a buyer will use; the shorter the extension, the less duration risk the buyer takes.
risks: The tenant may decline a short extension or demand a rent concession that offsets the benefit.
Timing risk: if the market turns before the extension ends, the window closes.
Two transaction events mean two sets of legal and advisory costs.

pathways.name: Hold to expiry, then re-tenant or reposition
pathways.summary: Run the lease out, then lease to another operator or redevelop the site.
drivers: Fast-food sites are small-footprint, high-visibility parcels that can often be re-let to another limited-service or service-retail user.
Los Angeles city contains 8,304.2 people per square mile, among the densest urban footprints in the United States, which supports a range of alternative uses.
The county added 22,250 building permits in 2025, indicating continuing construction activity.
risks: Vacancy, tenant-improvement and leasing-commission costs are entirely the owner's during a dark period, and no official source can estimate them for this site.
The 60% thirty-year likelihood of an M≥6.7 earthquake in the Los Angeles region is an uninsured-balance-sheet risk that is worst when the site is vacant.
Re-tenanting a purpose-built restaurant box can require capital the owner may not want to commit at this stage.
Los Angeles County population is 3.2% below its 2020 base, so re-leasing demand assumptions should not be optimistic.

Jack in the Box Inc. guided to 50 to 60 closures in fiscal 2026, reported a 6.8% decline in franchise rental revenue over 40 weeks, discontinued its dividend and buyback, and refinanced $500 million of securitised notes during fiscal 2026.
Site-level closure at or before expiry
The 'JACK on Track' plan is described as a block closure programme plus the sale of real estate. Whether this site is in the block cannot be determined without the lease and the operator's plan.
If the obligor is a single-unit franchisee rather than the public company, the credit behind the rent is materially weaker and the closure programme runs through that franchise agreement.
System same-store sales fell 1.1% in Q3 FY2026 on top of a 7.1% decline in the prior-year quarter, which supports a tenant asking for rent relief at renewal.
The ten-year Treasury moved between 4.77% and 5.31% between 2026-09-01 and 2026-11-05 and stood at 4.84% on 2026-11-05. Net-lease values are priced off this anchor.
Property-tax reassessment on sale or on a long lease
Proposition 13 resets base year value on a change in ownership, and a leasehold of 35 years or more including options is itself a change in ownership when created or terminated.
Inside the City of Los Angeles, a sale above $5,400,000 carries a total city transfer tax of 4.45% and a sale at or above $10,900,000 carries 5.95%, on the full consideration, plus 0.11% county tax.

California's fast-food minimum wage has been $20.00 per hour since April 1, 2024 and applies to franchisees; the state rate is $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026. Unit economics, and therefore rent coverage, are compressed by the higher floor.
Los Angeles County population is 3.2% below its April 2020 estimates base and the city is 0.8% below; population is not growing into new restaurant supply.
CPI-U in the Los Angeles metro area rose 3.7% year over year to September 2026, with energy up 20.3%, while the Employment Cost Index rose 3.9%. Real disposable income is being squeezed.
California's residential and commercial insurance market has been under stress following the January 2025 fires; no official source in this project quantifies the premium for this parcel.
One site, one operator, one intersection, in a system whose unit count fell by 13 net restaurants in a single quarter.
A like-kind exchange has statutory identification and closing deadlines and, since 2018, covers real property only. Missing a deadline defeats the deferral.

UCERF3 puts the 30-year likelihood of one or more M≥6.7 earthquakes in the Los Angeles region at 60%, of M≥7.0 at 46%, and of M≥7.5 at 31%. Earthquake is generally excluded from standard property policies.

CAL FIRE issued Local Responsibility Area fire hazard severity zone maps to jurisdictions in early 2025 and has the 2026 State Responsibility Area update in public comment. Central Los Angeles is not immune: the January 2025 fires destroyed large parts of the county.
FEMA's Map Service Center is the official determination point, but no flood zone could be established for this parcel without the address. Urban flooding is a documented Los Angeles County hazard.
Civil unrest or a prolonged local shock

No official source quantifies this probability for a specific parcel, so no number is asserted here. It is listed because a single-site retail asset has no internal diversification against a localised shutdown.
Rapid policy shift on property or transfer tax
Measure ULA thresholds are indexed annually and local tax measures are subject to the ballot. A change can alter after-tax proceeds between signing and closing.
